validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, operating interstate gas transmission pipeline, corroborated across CER (Canada Energy Regulator pipeline profile, apps.cer-rec.gc.ca, section updated Oct 2024), Enbridge's own 'Energy Infrastructure Assets' factsheet PDF, the operator's mnpp.com/US site + FAQ page, offshore-technology.com (GlobalData market-data page), and three Federal Register / PHMSA documents (1996 FERC NOI, 1996 FERC order notice, 2006 PHMSA waiver-request notice). PipelineType=transmission confirmed independently by mnpp.com ('684-mile transmission pipeline system') and offshore-technology.com ('owns and operates transmission pipeline system'). No duplicate risk: no other PID in the US gas roster covers this system. CAVEAT 1 -- CROSS-BORDER SCOPE (orchestrator framing correction): the task brief characterized this row as 'the US portion' of a cross-border system. That is NOT what the sheet records: GEM's own StartLocation/StartCountryOrArea = Goldboro, Nova Scotia, Canada and EndLocation/EndCountryOrArea = Dracut, Massachusetts, United States (confirmed via the live GEM CSV, sheet row 70), and LengthKnown=1432 km / Capacity=830 MMcf/d are WHOLE-SYSTEM figures (Enbridge's factsheet states the identical 1,432 km / '889 miles' total, split as US 552 km + Canada 880 km). So P0212 is the ENTIRE binational M&NP system in one row, not a US-only segment -- there is no companion Canada-only PID on this roster. This is not a data defect (the recorded endpoints and totals are internally consistent and well-sourced), just a correction to how the row should be read; every fill below states explicitly which country/segment each individual source describes so a reviewer is never left assuming a Canada-only or US-only figure covers the whole row. CAVEAT 2 -- FLOW REVERSAL: CER states offshore Nova Scotia gas (ExxonMobil's Sable Offshore Energy Project from late 1999, Encana's Deep Panuke from 2013) supplied the line until production ended in 2018; 'Since 2019, the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline (M&NP) transports natural gas imported from the U.S. Production may include U.S. basins such as Appalachia or Canada's W[estern Canada]' -- i.e. the physical flow direction reversed (now south-to-north into the Maritimes) even though the pipeline's physical start/end points are unchanged, consistent with mnpp.com/US's own statement that flow 'currently...from south to north as the offshore Nova Scotia gas supply is permanently shut-in.' Per the brief's specific guidance for this row, the start location (Goldboro) is NOT moved despite the reversal -- confirmed correct as recorded. CAVEAT 3 -- minor scope-defined length discrepancy: mnpp.com/US states a '684-mile transmission pipeline system' total, while Enbridge's factsheet states 889 miles (1,432 km) total -- exactly matching the sheet's recorded 1432 km. mnpp.com separately describes a jointly-owned 101-mile 'Joint Facilities' segment (co-owned with Portland Natural Gas Transmission System) and a separate Methuen-to-Beverly MA extension, which are plausibly excluded from the 684-mile figure but included in Enbridge's 889-mile system total; this is treated as a definitional-scope difference, not a material conflict, because the more precise Enbridge figure is independently corroborated component-by-component (CER: Canada-only 878-880 km; offshore-technology.com: US-only 552 km; 878+552=1430, within rounding of 1432). CAPACITY: no source states '830' literally (checked via full-text grep of the Enbridge factsheet PDF); Enbridge states 'approximately 0.8 Bcf/d' aggregate (US 0.8 Bcf/d + Canada 0.5 Bcf/d, which are NOT simply additive since Canada's throughput is now bidirectional/reduced post-2018) -- 830 MMcf/d is within rounding of 0.8 Bcf/d and is treated as REFS_ADDED at medium tier per rule 7 (agreement within rounding), not a material spec concern.

fills.researcher_notes: Reclassified from UNRESOLVED by the orchestrator: rule 4(e) reserves UNRESOLVED for units where NOTHING was found, and two independent origins (the 1996 FERC application via the U.S. Federal Register, and the Canada Energy Regulator pipeline profile) both name the Sable Offshore Energy Project as this system's upstream supply. CURRENCY CAVEAT, which is why this is staged as CONTESTED rather than a clean fill and why the tier is medium: Sable ceased production in 2018 and CER states the line has run in reverse since 2019, importing gas with no single named upstream facility, so the sourced value is the original design source and not the present one. A reviewer should decide between recording the historical source with a note and leaving the cell blank; the flow-reversal finding is carried in this shard's validity record. Leaving this UNRESOLVED rather than filling it, despite finding two independent, well-corroborated sources for the ORIGINAL/design fuel source: both the 1996 FERC application (Sable Offshore Energy Project delivery system) and CER's pipeline profile name 'Sable Offshore Energy Project' (plus Encana's Deep Panuke, from 2013) as the historical upstream supply. The problem is currency, not sourcing: CER explicitly states that supply source stopped in 2018 and since 2019 the pipeline has been running in the reverse direction, importing gas with no single named upstream facility ('may include U.S. basins such as Appalachia or Canada's Western [Canada]'). A FuelSource field is understood on this tracker as naming a specific field/plant/facility feeding the line; entering 'Sable Offshore Energy Project' without heavy qualification would misrepresent the CURRENT (2019-present) supply arrangement, and there is no single current facility name to substitute. Recommend a human decision on whether FuelSource should carry the historical/original value with a caveat, or stay blank -- documenting both well-sourced options here rather than picking one unilaterally.

FERC's 1996 filing (docket CP96-809/810, Federal Register Vol. 61 No. 202) states a staged construction cost of 'about $63 million' (1998 stage, 42.1 mi) plus 'about $341 million' (1999 stage) = roughly $404 million total FOR THAT DOCKET ONLY (the Phase II mainline + laterals, ~229.6 mi of 24-in + 1.8 mi of 30-in mainline + 154 mi of laterals) -- this excludes the separate Phase I facilities (Dracut-Wells, 66 mi, docket CP96-178) and any of the later Phase III (2003)/Phase IV (2008) expansion costs (EIA-sourced: Phase III $133.99M, Phase IV $321.3M -- both separate expansion projects, not part of the original system's build cost). Since SegmentCost should describe the cost of the physical scope recorded on this row (the whole original 1999 system, Goldboro-Dracut), and I could not find a single source stating that whole-system total (as opposed to one docket's partial scope), this is left UNRESOLVED rather than reporting a partial figure as if it were the total.
